newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TALKS AVERT HUNTER VALLEY COAL STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: TALKS AVERT HUNTER VALLEY COAL STRIKE.

text.p: A threatened strike at Coal and Allied Industries Ltd's Hunter Valley No 1 coking and thermal coal mine was averted by a recommendation of the Australian Industrial Relations Commission (AIRC) on Tuesday.
The AIRC recommended that negotiations continue between CAIL and the Construction, Forestry Mining and Energy Union (CFMEU) for another 21 days.
The same terms and conditions would apply as the last 21 days of negotiations, Justice Alan Boulton said.
The CFMEU would hold a meeting with its members on Wednesday morning, Tony Maher, senior general vice president of CFMEU, said after the AIRC's recommendation was handed down.
The AIRC recommendation was expected to be agreed to by members, he said.
Before the AIRC's recommendation, the CFMEU had planned that a new strike would begin on Tuesday morning. This would follow a return to work on July 22 after a bitter six week strike.
Justice Boulton said he did not see negotiations between CFMEU and CAIL going on forever.
A CAIL official said hopefully there would be no strike.
"It would be disappointing (if a strike now occurred)," he said.
"We refute allegations made that the company is acting provocatively," a company official told the AIRC.

The mine produces coking and thermal coal for Japanese and other Asian customers. It has daily production of about 25,000 tonnes, with one million tonnes of output disrupted in the last strike. CAIL is a 70 percent-owned subsidiary of Rio Tinto Ltd.
